answer.answer:
Site-specific phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporin NUP98 initiates nuclear-import failure that secondarily increases cytoplasmic TDP-43 in TDP-43 proteinopathy models of ALS

This proposal tests that claim in TDP-43 proteinopathy models. Phosphorylation of NUP98 at FG-adjacent serine or threonine residues is the candidate initiating nuclear-pore lesion. Selective import failure is proposed to precede, and then to amplify, cytoplasmic TDP-43 accumulation. Calling NUP98 an FG-nucleoporin rests on unverified prior knowledge. Supplied sources support pore and transport dysfunction in defined contexts. They do not establish nucleoporin phosphorylation as a cause.

Supported premises. Disease-linked TDP-43 associates with insoluble nuclear-pore and transport components, disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cells, and is accompanied by pore pathology in ALS tissue [S1]. Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA is linked to RanGAP mislocalization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons, and manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modify those phenotypes [S2]. That C9orf72 route is genetic-context-specific [S2]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can arise independently of conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport-associated proteins, and track with import failure, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death [S3]. Phosphorylated TDP-43 in those assemblies is a modification of TDP-43, and [S3] is silent on nucleoporin phosphorylation. Cellular stress can recruit transport factors into stress granules and impair nucleocytoplasmic transport, and altering stress-granule assembly can modify transport defects and disease-model phenotypes [S4]. Read together, [S3] and [S4] show that transport-factor sequestration is a credible alternative and that conventional stress granules are dispensable for some TDP-43-linked transport defects.

Speculative bridges. The substrate choice, the FG-adjacent residues, and the kinase are assumptions. Unverified prior knowledge holds that phosphates on FG-nucleoporins can change local charge and barrier interactions, and that TDP-43 nuclear entry uses a classical nuclear-localization signal and karyopherins. No supplied source identifies NUP98, a residue, or a kinase. Sites remain unspecified until mass spectrometry maps them. TDP-43 localization can report barrier function only after the phosphate mark is measured directly.

Initiating mechanism versus downstream response. The initiating step is phosphorylation of pore-resident NUP98 during early stress that accompanies emerging TDP-43 pathology. The downstream response is reduced karyopherin import, loss of nuclear TDP-43, and increased cytoplasmic TDP-43, which can then worsen pore composition [S1] and sustain transport failure [S3]. In this ordering, cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies and stress-granule capture of transport factors are later amplifiers.

Alternative explanations. Transport-factor capture inside stress granules can impair import by itself [S4]. Recruitment of transport proteins into stress-granule-independent TDP-43 assemblies can impair import as well [S3]. In C9orf72-repeat neurons, RanGAP mislocalization can be the primary import lesion [S2]. Broader proteotoxic stress can injure pores and leave any detected phosphate as a late correlate of injury.

Discriminating preclinical strategy. Timed sampling is performed in neurons induced to form cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies, following the logic of [S3], and in C9orf72-repeat neurons, following [S2]. Mass spectrometry maps NUP98 phosphosites in the same samples used for functional assays. Abundance-matched phospho-null NUP98 is introduced under conditions that still allow stress granules and cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies. Preserved import-reporter flux and preserved nuclear TDP-43 favor a required NUP98 phosphate; continued import failure favors sequestration [S3][S4]. In a second arm, phosphomimetic NUP98 is expressed before a stress trigger and before TDP-43 assemblies. Early import failure followed by rising cytoplasmic TDP-43 favors sufficiency of the phosphate mark. In a third arm, stress-granule assembly is forced while NUP98 cannot be phosphorylated. Preserved transport favors the phosphorylation hypothesis; transport failure favors the [S4] account. In C9orf72-repeat neurons, NUP98 phosphorylation is ordered against RanGAP localization. Import failure with unmodified NUP98 assigns that genetic context to the [S2] pathway. Each culture is scored for import rate, nuclear-to-cytoplasmic TDP-43 ratio, RanGAP localization, stress-granule markers, and NUP98 phosphate occupancy so that temporal order is observed.

Falsifying observation. In the TDP-43 proteinopathy model, indistinguishable kinetics of import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and later cell death with phospho-null and wild-type NUP98, while sequestration routes remain intact, falsifies necessity. Intact import and intact nuclear TDP-43 after phosphomimetic NUP98, in the absence of those assemblies, falsifies sufficiency. Absence of detectable NUP98 phosphorylation at a time when transport is already impaired is a further falsifier. Rescue that tracks only with a change in NUP98 abundance or pore number, after abundance matching, falsifies a site-specific phosphate switch.

Limitations. The kinase, the sites, and the focus on NUP98 are assumptions based on unverified prior knowledge. A positive result in TDP-43 proteinopathy models would leave sporadic ALS and many C9orf72 trajectories unresolved [S1][S2]. Acute NUP98 mutants can obstruct pores through mass action. Cross-sectional human tissue cannot order phosphorylation relative to transport failure, so discrimination rests on the preclinical time series. A NUP98 phosphate could coexist with sequestration [S4] or RanGAP redistribution [S2] as a parallel lesion. The experiment asks whether NUP98 phosphorylation is necessary and sufficient to initiate import failure in one modeled setting. It does not claim a validated disease mechanism or a treatment.

A second assumption is that those phosphates slow facilitated import enough to restrict TDP-43 re-entry and deepen nuclear depletion. The kinase is assumed to respond to the assemblies or their local stress, a path distinct from repeat RNA in [S2]. None of [S1]-[S4] names the kinase, the sites, or this order.

Nup98 phosphorylation at the nuclear pore initiates selective nuclear-import failure and nuclear TDP-43 depletion in TDP-43 proteinopathy models of ALS

Hypothesis. In neurons developing TDP-43 proteinopathy, phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 inside otherwise intact nuclear pore complexes is an early pore-intrinsic event that reduces karyopherin-facilitated nuclear import. Import failure then depletes nuclear TDP-43, favors persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies, and contributes to neuronal dysfunction. The proposed scope is experimental TDP-43 proteinopathy, with a parallel test in C9orf72-repeat neurons. The same sequence is not assumed for every ALS genotype.

Supported premises. Insoluble TDP-43 aggregates associate with nuclear-pore and transport components; disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nucleocytoplasmic transport in cell systems, and related pore pathology is present in ALS tissue [S1]. These observations support a TDP-43–transport connection and leave the initiating biochemical event unspecified [S1]. Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA is linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons, and manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modify model phenotypes [S2]. That route is genetic-context-specific and does not establish a shared mechanism for sporadic ALS or a nucleoporin phosphorylation step [S2]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form independently of conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport-associated proteins, and accompany impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and cell death [S3]. Phosphorylated TDP-43 within those assemblies documents a modification of TDP-43, which is separate from nucleoporin phosphorylation [S3]. Cellular stress can also recruit transport factors into stress granules and impair transport, and altering stress-granule assembly modifies transport defects and disease-model phenotypes [S4]. Together, [S3] and [S4] show that transport failure can accompany either stress-granule sequestration or stress-granule-independent TDP-43 assemblies. No supplied source establishes nucleoporin phosphorylation as an ALS-initiating cause.

Speculative bridges. The kinase, the modified residues, and a direct biophysical effect on the pore are assumptions. Unverified prior knowledge: Nup98 is an FG-nucleoporin, and phosphorylation by mitotic or stress-responsive kinases can change NPC permeability in non-ALS systems; TDP-43 carries a classical nuclear-localization sequence and is imported by karyopherin-family receptors. The assumed chain is that proteotoxic or stress signaling phosphorylates Nup98 at FG-adjacent sites, selectively weakening facilitated import of NLS cargos, including TDP-43, while early passive pore integrity remains largely preserved. A further assumption is that this modification can precede, and be separated from, RanGAP mislocalization [S2], transport-factor sequestration in stress granules [S4], and recruitment of transport proteins into cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies [S3]. Under the hypothesis, nuclear TDP-43 loss, expansion of cytoplasmic assemblies, broader transport collapse, and cell death are downstream responses [S1], [S3].

Alternative explanations. Alternative A: stress-granule sequestration of transport factors is the cause of import failure, and Nup98 phosphorylation is a later correlate of stress [S4]. Alternative B: stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing is sufficient to mislocalize transport factors and inhibit import, so pore phosphorylation follows assembly [S3]. Alternative C: in C9orf72 models, repeat RNA acts through RanGAP localization, and Nup98 phosphorylation is dispensable [S2]. Alternative D: nucleoporin mislocalization reported with TDP-43 pathology reflects secondary NPC injury after prolonged stress, and phosphorylation marks damaged pores after import has already failed [S1].

Discriminating preclinical test. In human iPSC-derived motor neurons expressing an ALS-linked TDP-43 variant, and in a matched C9orf72-repeat neuron model, sample a time course that ends before frank cell death. At each point measure Nup98 phosphorylation by mass spectrometry or a validated phospho-specific reagent, NLS-reporter import rates, nuclear versus cytoplasmic TDP-43, G3BP1-positive stress granules, and localization of RanGAP and representative karyopherins. Three perturbations separate the hypothesis from the alternatives. A CRISPR knock-in phospho-deficient Nup98 allele, with candidate serines and threonines replaced by alanine, is predicted to preserve early NLS import and nuclear TDP-43 even if stress granules or cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies still form. A phospho-mimetic Nup98 allele introduced into otherwise unstressed neurons is predicted to impair NLS import and lower nuclear TDP-43 in the absence of stress-granule induction and RanGAP sequestration. Genetic disruption of stress-granule assembly is predicted to leave early Nup98 phosphorylation and the import defect in place if pore phosphorylation is initiating, whereas Alternative A predicts restoration of import when stress granules are prevented [S4]. Temporal order is part of the test: initiating phosphorylation must precede nuclear TDP-43 depletion. Running the same panel in the C9orf72 line asks whether that genotype shares the Nup98 step or proceeds through the RanGAP route [S2].

Falsifying observation. The hypothesis is falsified if Nup98 phosphorylation is detected only after NLS-import failure and nuclear TDP-43 loss; if phospho-deficient Nup98 leaves the early import defect unchanged while stress-granule disruption or restoration of RanGAP localization rescues import; or if phospho-mimetic Nup98 leaves NLS import and nuclear TDP-43 intact in unstressed neurons. Rescue that tracks the release of transport factors from granules or from TDP-43 assemblies, independently of the Nup98 phospho-state, would support Alternatives A–C instead.

Limitations. Kinase identity, the site map, and the effect on FG-repeat interactions lie outside [S1]–[S4] and remain assumptions. Phospho-mimetic substitutions only approximate a phosphate. iPSC motor neurons compress a long human disease course into a short culture window. Findings restricted to TDP-43 and C9orf72 models would leave ALS without TDP-43 proteinopathy unresolved. Nucleoporin redundancy can mask a single-site allele, and phospho-reagent specificity requires orthogonal mass spectrometry. The design tests a causal hypothesis in preclinical models and does not validate a treatment.

answer.answer:
Nup98 phosphorylation as a downstream amplifier of nuclear-import failure after cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly in ALS/FTD-relevant neurons

In C9orf72-negative human neurons that form ALS/FTD-type cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies, proline-directed phosphorylation of NPC-incorporated Nup98 is proposed to amplify an earlier nuclear-import deficit, deepen nuclear TDP-43 loss, and promote cell death. The causal agent is phosphorylation at proline-directed sites occupied on isolated NPCs. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing is the initiating event. Pore-resident Nup98 phosphorylation is a later change of assembled pores, separable from transport-factor sequestration and from import failure that follows Nup98 exit.

Insoluble TDP-43 aggregates associate with nuclear-pore and transport components, and disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and transport in cells, with related pore pathology in ALS tissue. This supports a TDP-43-to-transport inquiry and leaves nucleoporin phosphorylation unidentified [S1]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form without conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport proteins, and accompany import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and cell death; phosphorylated TDP-43 in those assemblies is not nucleoporin phosphorylation [S3]. Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA impairs import through RanGAP mislocalization [S2]. Stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs transport, and changing stress-granule assembly modifies that phenotype [S4]. With [S3], conventional stress granules are dispensable for some TDP-43-linked defects.

Kinase identity, sites, and order are assumptions. Unverified prior knowledge: Nup98 is a central-channel FG-nucleoporin; mitotic CDK1 marks human Nup98 on a fuller set of S/T-P sites than S591, S595, S822, and S861; mitotic CDK1 is a weak default in post-mitotic neurons. The speculative bridge is a limited proline-directed mark on NPC-incorporated Nup98 after assemblies form, sufficient to slow facilitated import and restrict TDP-43 re-entry. [S1]–[S4] name no kinase, cluster, or order. Isolated-NPC mass spectrometry confirms occupancy before alleles are built. Occupied sites are compared with the fuller mitotic map, and only NPC-incorporated sites define the phospho-deficient and phospho-mimetic alleles.

Sequestration in stress granules [S4] or in TDP-43 assemblies [S3] can impair import with no Nup98 phosphate. In expansion carriers, RanGAP mislocalization can explain import failure [S2]. Phospho-Nup98 can report stress-kinase activity in proteotoxic injury. Nup98 exit, within the [S1] premise, can reduce import without a gating phosphate on assembled pores.

The test uses C9orf72-negative human iPSC-derived motor neurons. Blue light at T0 induces Cry2olig–TDP-43 (method: unverified prior knowledge) into persistent cytoplasmic assemblies of the [S3] class. Light-only and Cry2olig-only arms run in parallel. Assays at 2, 6, 24, and 72 h record assemblies, G3BP1 granules, Nup98 colocalization with a scaffold nucleoporin, NLS/NES import rate as nuclear accumulation per minute and nucleus/cytoplasm ratio, nuclear TDP-43, cell death, and NPC phospho-stoichiometry. Readout is targeted MS of occupied sites, site antibodies only after peptide confirmation, a pilot-set cell-input minimum, and an FDR/decoy rule that rejects off-pore spectra and misassigned FG-nucleoporin peptides. Baseline stoichiometry defines the pre-phosphate window; the first pre-registered rise opens the phospho window.

A pilot in these neurons estimates import-rate SD and the de-mixing effect size. Amplifier slowing versus the pre-phosphate window must exceed a pre-registered multiple of that SD, while Nup98–scaffold colocalization stays within pilot noise of baseline. Phosphate confined to departing Nup98 counts as [S1] mislocalization.

The causal allele is introduced during NPC biogenesis, before T0, by CRISPR knock-in or doxycycline-inducible replacement, and incorporation is quantified by targeted MS. Rescue is interpreted only above a pilot-derived incorporation floor, as a pre-registered fraction of the incremental import-rate loss and nuclear TDP-43 drop, with assembly load within pilot noise of the pathological control. Nup98 residence is measured in the same neurons by FRAP or pulse-SILAC on isolated NPCs before any post-assembly window is locked. A post-T0 replacement arm is opened only when measured residence fits that window. Causal inference uses the occupied-site allele. After occupancy, analog-sensitive CDK1, CDK5, and MAPK tests (candidates: unverified prior knowledge) ask which enzyme writes the mark.

The stress-granule arm removes G3BP1, a granule nucleator (unverified prior knowledge), by knockout or an assembly-deficient mutant and is confirmed by loss of G3BP1-positive granules. Persisting NPC phospho-Nup98 plus the late deficit in remaining assemblies aligns the mark with the [S3] route. Phospho-mimetic Nup98 without TDP-43 pathology tests pore autonomy: slower short-window import and little new insoluble TDP-43.

Falsifying observations: unoccupied sites on NPC-incorporated Nup98 across import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and death, or phosphate only off the pore; phospho-deficient Nup98, once above the incorporation floor, leaves incremental import loss and nuclear TDP-43 loss matching the pathological baseline while assemblies persist; a window gap below the pilot threshold; phospho-Nup98 before TDP-43 redistribution; or a full assembly and death sequence from the phospho-mimetic allele alone, which would reclassify the mark as initiating.

Limitations: sites, kinase candidates, turnover, delivery performance, and Cry2olig details are unverified prior knowledge outside [S1]–[S4]. Phospho-mimetics approximate phosphate. iPSC motor neurons omit long human aging and other ALS subtypes. Other FG-nucleoporins may compensate, and a misassigned peptide could imitate an NPC signal.
